More data clearly helps. Going from 99 to 199 stays, the held-out R² rose:

| Target | 99 stays | 199 stays |
|---|---|---|
| Insulin residual, 1 h before the reading | 0.13 | 0.37 |
| Insulin residual, 2 h before | 0.14 | 0.22 |
| Combined insulin correction target | −0.03 | 0.35 |
| Norepinephrine shock, 1 h before | 0.11 | 0.13 |

So the ridge probe is data-limited, not limited by the encoding, and more state passes are worth spending.

The norepinephrine shock is barely decodable. For that drug I will probably use a different target, the rate minus the rate implied by the MAP readings alone, which keeps the carried-over part of earlier shocks.

This pass requests states for the next 100 of my 300 selected stays.
